History, Evolution & Scope of Surgery.question: 1) Father of Surgery is:
History, Evolution & Scope of Surgery.exp: Sushruta is regarded as the Father of Surgery and described numerous operative procedures in the Sushruta Samhita.

History, Evolution & Scope of Surgery.question: 2) Father of modern antiseptic surgery is:
History, Evolution & Scope of Surgery.exp: Lister introduced carbolic acid for antisepsis, markedly reducing postoperative infection.

History, Evolution & Scope of Surgery.question: 3) Ether was first successfully used as a surgical anaesthetic by:
History, Evolution & Scope of Surgery.exp: William T. G. Morton publicly demonstrated ether anaesthesia in 1846.

History, Evolution & Scope of Surgery.question: 4) The first successful human heart transplantation was performed by:
History, Evolution & Scope of Surgery.exp: Christian Barnard performed the first successful human heart transplant in 1967.

History, Evolution & Scope of Surgery.question: 5) The specialty primarily concerned with diseases requiring operative intervention is:
History, Evolution & Scope of Surgery.exp: Surgery involves diagnosis, operative treatment and perioperative care of surgical diseases.

History, Evolution & Scope of Surgery.question: 6) Which is NOT a principle of modern surgical practice?
History, Evolution & Scope of Surgery.exp: Early diagnosis and timely intervention improve surgical outcomes.

History, Evolution & Scope of Surgery.question: 7) Before elective surgery, the most important initial step is:
History, Evolution & Scope of Surgery.exp: History and examination guide risk assessment and further investigations.

History, Evolution & Scope of Surgery.question: 8) The ASA classification is used to assess:
History, Evolution & Scope of Surgery.exp: ASA (American Society of Anesthesiologists) physical status grading predicts perioperative risk.

History, Evolution & Scope of Surgery.question: 9) ASA Grade I patient is:
History, Evolution & Scope of Surgery.exp: ASA I indicates a normal healthy individual.

History, Evolution & Scope of Surgery.question: 10) Which ASA grade denotes a moribund patient not expected to survive without surgery?
History, Evolution & Scope of Surgery.exp: ASA V patients are critically ill and unlikely to survive without the operation.

History, Evolution & Scope of Surgery.question: 11) The suffix “E” in ASA classification indicates:
History, Evolution & Scope of Surgery.exp: “E” is added to denote emergency operations.

History, Evolution & Scope of Surgery.question: 12) Which investigation is routinely required before most major elective operations?
History, Evolution & Scope of Surgery.exp: CBC helps detect anaemia, infection and thrombocytopenia.

History, Evolution & Scope of Surgery.question: 13) Which patient requires blood grouping and cross-matching before surgery?
History, Evolution & Scope of Surgery.option4: Major operation with anticipated blood loss
History, Evolution & Scope of Surgery.exp: Cross-matching is indicated when significant blood loss is expected.

History, Evolution & Scope of Surgery.question: 14) The most common cause of postoperative pulmonary complications is:
History, Evolution & Scope of Surgery.exp: Atelectasis commonly develops in the early postoperative period due to shallow breathing and impaired coughing.

History, Evolution & Scope of Surgery.question: 15) Smoking should ideally be stopped before elective surgery for at least:
History, Evolution & Scope of Surgery.exp: Smoking cessation for at least 4 weeks improves pulmonary and wound outcomes.

History, Evolution & Scope of Surgery.question: 16) Which of the following increases the risk of postoperative wound infection?
History, Evolution & Scope of Surgery.exp: Smoking impairs tissue oxygenation and wound healing.

History, Evolution & Scope of Surgery.question: 17) The most effective measure to reduce surgical site infection is:
History, Evolution & Scope of Surgery.exp: Proper asepsis remains the cornerstone of preventing surgical site infection.

History, Evolution & Scope of Surgery.question: 18) Informed consent must be obtained:
History, Evolution & Scope of Surgery.exp: Valid consent requires capacity, adequate information and voluntariness.

History, Evolution & Scope of Surgery.question: 19) Which of the following is NOT an essential element of informed consent?
History, Evolution & Scope of Surgery.exp: A magistrate is not routinely required for valid surgical consent.

History, Evolution & Scope of Surgery.question: 20) Which electrolyte abnormality should preferably be corrected before elective surgery?
History, Evolution & Scope of Surgery.exp: Severe hypokalaemia predisposes to cardiac arrhythmias and should be corrected.

History, Evolution & Scope of Surgery.question: 21) The purpose of preoperative fasting is to reduce:
History, Evolution & Scope of Surgery.exp: Fasting reduces gastric volume and acidity, lowering aspiration risk.

History, Evolution & Scope of Surgery.question: 22) Prophylactic antibiotics are most effective when administered:
History, Evolution & Scope of Surgery.exp: Maximum tissue concentration at the time of incision provides optimal prophylaxis.

History, Evolution & Scope of Surgery.question: 23) Which patient has the highest risk of venous thromboembolism?
History, Evolution & Scope of Surgery.exp: Advanced age, trauma and immobility markedly increase VTE risk.

History, Evolution & Scope of Surgery.question: 24) The best method to reduce postoperative deep vein thrombosis is:
History, Evolution & Scope of Surgery.exp: Early ambulation is one of the most effective measures for DVT prevention.

History, Evolution & Scope of Surgery.question: 25) Which factor is most important for successful elective surgery?
History, Evolution & Scope of Surgery.exp: Appropriate assessment and optimization before surgery significantly improve outcomes.

History, Evolution & Scope of Surgery.question: 26) Which patient requires the most extensive preoperative cardiac evaluation?
History, Evolution & Scope of Surgery.exp: Advanced age, diabetes and previous MI significantly increase perioperative cardiac risk.

History, Evolution & Scope of Surgery.question: 27) The most important purpose of preoperative assessment is to:
History, Evolution & Scope of Surgery.option4: Identify and optimize correctable risk factors
History, Evolution & Scope of Surgery.exp: Proper optimization before surgery decreases perioperative morbidity and mortality.

History, Evolution & Scope of Surgery.question: 28) Which investigation is routinely performed before blood transfusion?
History, Evolution & Scope of Surgery.exp: Cross-matching minimizes transfusion reactions by ensuring compatibility.

History, Evolution & Scope of Surgery.question: 29) Which condition is associated with poor wound healing?
History, Evolution & Scope of Surgery.exp: Diabetes impairs leukocyte function, collagen synthesis and tissue perfusion.

History, Evolution & Scope of Surgery.question: 30) The most important reason for obtaining informed consent is:
History, Evolution & Scope of Surgery.exp: Consent respects patient autonomy and is an essential medico-legal requirement.

History, Evolution & Scope of Surgery.question: 31) Which of the following patients has the highest risk of postoperative pulmonary complications?
History, Evolution & Scope of Surgery.exp: Age, smoking and chronic lung disease markedly increase pulmonary complications.

History, Evolution & Scope of Surgery.question: 32) Which of the following is NOT usually a routine preoperative investigation in a healthy young patient undergoing minor surgery?
History, Evolution & Scope of Surgery.exp: Routine chest radiography is not recommended in healthy asymptomatic individuals.

History, Evolution & Scope of Surgery.question: 33) Functional capacity before surgery is commonly expressed in:
History, Evolution & Scope of Surgery.exp: Functional capacity is commonly assessed using metabolic equivalents (METs).

History, Evolution & Scope of Surgery.question: 34) Which ASA class describes a patient with severe systemic disease that limits activity but is not incapacitating?
History, Evolution & Scope of Surgery.exp: ASA III indicates severe systemic disease with functional limitation.

History, Evolution & Scope of Surgery.question: 35) Which ASA class represents severe systemic disease that is a constant threat to life?
History, Evolution & Scope of Surgery.exp: ASA IV patients have severe disease with significant perioperative risk.

History, Evolution & Scope of Surgery.question: 36) Which medication is commonly continued until the day of surgery?
History, Evolution & Scope of Surgery.exp: Chronic beta-blockers are generally continued to reduce cardiovascular complications.

History, Evolution & Scope of Surgery.question: 37) Which patient is most likely to require perioperative antibiotic prophylaxis?
History, Evolution & Scope of Surgery.exp: Colorectal surgery has a high risk of bacterial contamination.

History, Evolution & Scope of Surgery.question: 38) Which factor increases the risk of aspiration during induction of anaesthesia?
History, Evolution & Scope of Surgery.exp: Gastric contents increase the risk of aspiration pneumonitis.

History, Evolution & Scope of Surgery.question: 39) The ideal time to assess airway before surgery is:
History, Evolution & Scope of Surgery.exp: Airway assessment predicts potential difficulty with intubation.

History, Evolution & Scope of Surgery.question: 40) Which one is NOT a component of the WHO Surgical Safety Checklist?
History, Evolution & Scope of Surgery.exp: The WHO checklist includes Sign In, Time Out and Sign Out.

History, Evolution & Scope of Surgery.question: 41) The principal aim of the WHO Surgical Safety Checklist is:
History, Evolution & Scope of Surgery.option4: Reduce complications and improve patient safety
History, Evolution & Scope of Surgery.exp: It improves communication and reduces preventable surgical errors.

History, Evolution & Scope of Surgery.question: 42) Which investigation is most useful for assessing coagulation before surgery?
History, Evolution & Scope of Surgery.exp: PT/INR evaluates the extrinsic coagulation pathway and anticoagulation status.

History, Evolution & Scope of Surgery.question: 43) Which patient has the greatest risk of postoperative wound infection?
History, Evolution & Scope of Surgery.exp: Contaminated emergency surgery has the highest infection risk.

History, Evolution & Scope of Surgery.question: 44) Which condition should ideally be corrected before elective surgery?
History, Evolution & Scope of Surgery.exp: Severe anaemia increases perioperative morbidity and should be corrected whenever possible.

History, Evolution & Scope of Surgery.question: 45) Which is the commonest cause of cancellation of elective surgery?
History, Evolution & Scope of Surgery.exp: Uncontrolled medical conditions frequently necessitate postponement of surgery.

History, Evolution & Scope of Surgery.question: 46) Which of the following decreases postoperative pulmonary complications?
History, Evolution & Scope of Surgery.exp: These measures improve lung expansion and reduce atelectasis.

History, Evolution & Scope of Surgery.question: 47) Which vitamin deficiency most impairs wound healing?
History, Evolution & Scope of Surgery.exp: Vitamin C is essential for collagen synthesis and normal wound repair.

History, Evolution & Scope of Surgery.question: 48) Serum albumin is commonly used as an indicator of:
History, Evolution & Scope of Surgery.exp: Hypoalbuminaemia is associated with poor nutritional status and increased postoperative complications.

History, Evolution & Scope of Surgery.question: 49) Which patient has the highest risk for postoperative DVT?
History, Evolution & Scope of Surgery.option4: Elderly obese patient after hip surgery
History, Evolution & Scope of Surgery.exp: Age, obesity, major orthopaedic surgery and immobility are major risk factors.

History, Evolution & Scope of Surgery.question: 50) Which measure is most effective in reducing perioperative mortality?
History, Evolution & Scope of Surgery.option1: Routine postoperative antibiotics for all surgeries
History, Evolution & Scope of Surgery.option3: Routine ICU admission for every patient
History, Evolution & Scope of Surgery.option4: Proper patient selection, optimization and safe surgical practice
History, Evolution & Scope of Surgery.exp: Good preoperative assessment, optimization, adherence to safety protocols and appropriate postoperative care have the greatest impact on reducing perioperative mortality.

History, Evolution & Scope of Surgery.question: 51) Which patient is most likely to require postoperative ICU care?
History, Evolution & Scope of Surgery.option1: Patient with severe sepsis undergoing emergency laparotomy
History, Evolution & Scope of Surgery.exp: Emergency major surgery in critically ill patients often requires postoperative intensive monitoring.

History, Evolution & Scope of Surgery.question: 52) The most common cause of perioperative myocardial infarction is:
History, Evolution & Scope of Surgery.option2: Increased myocardial oxygen demand in patients with coronary artery disease
History, Evolution & Scope of Surgery.exp: Patients with underlying coronary artery disease are at greatest risk during the perioperative period.

History, Evolution & Scope of Surgery.question: 53) Which investigation is most useful in assessing renal function before major surgery?
History, Evolution & Scope of Surgery.exp: Serum creatinine is routinely used to assess renal function and guide perioperative management.

History, Evolution & Scope of Surgery.question: 54) Which patient is most likely to require preoperative pulmonary function testing?
History, Evolution & Scope of Surgery.option2: Healthy woman undergoing breast lump excision
History, Evolution & Scope of Surgery.option4: Smoker with COPD scheduled for thoracotomy
History, Evolution & Scope of Surgery.exp: Pulmonary function tests help assess respiratory reserve before major thoracic surgery.

History, Evolution & Scope of Surgery.question: 55) Which factor is associated with increased postoperative mortality?
History, Evolution & Scope of Surgery.exp: Emergency operations generally carry higher morbidity and mortality than elective procedures.

History, Evolution & Scope of Surgery.question: 56) The commonest cause of postoperative fever during the first 24 hours is:
History, Evolution & Scope of Surgery.exp: Early postoperative fever is most commonly related to atelectasis rather than infection.

History, Evolution & Scope of Surgery.question: 57) Which patient has the highest risk of postoperative wound dehiscence?
History, Evolution & Scope of Surgery.exp: Diabetes, malnutrition and major abdominal surgery increase the risk of wound failure.

History, Evolution & Scope of Surgery.question: 58) Which of the following is NOT a modifiable preoperative risk factor?
History, Evolution & Scope of Surgery.exp: Age cannot be modified, although associated comorbidities can be optimized.

History, Evolution & Scope of Surgery.question: 59) The primary purpose of preoperative optimisation is to:
History, Evolution & Scope of Surgery.exp: Correcting reversible abnormalities reduces perioperative complications.

History, Evolution & Scope of Surgery.question: 60) Which condition is an absolute indication to postpone elective surgery?
History, Evolution & Scope of Surgery.exp: Life-threatening metabolic abnormalities must be corrected before elective surgery.

History, Evolution & Scope of Surgery.question: 61) Which blood component should be available before major vascular surgery?
History, Evolution & Scope of Surgery.exp: Major vascular procedures carry a significant risk of blood loss.

History, Evolution & Scope of Surgery.question: 62) Which patient has the greatest risk of aspiration during anaesthesia?
History, Evolution & Scope of Surgery.exp: Gastric distension and delayed emptying increase aspiration risk.

History, Evolution & Scope of Surgery.question: 63) A patient refuses surgery despite understanding the consequences. The surgeon should:
History, Evolution & Scope of Surgery.option4: Ask relatives to overrule the patient
History, Evolution & Scope of Surgery.exp: A competent adult has the right to refuse treatment.

History, Evolution & Scope of Surgery.question: 64) Which principle is most important during communication before surgery?
History, Evolution & Scope of Surgery.option3: Honest discussion of benefits, risks and alternatives
History, Evolution & Scope of Surgery.exp: Proper counselling is essential for valid informed consent.

History, Evolution & Scope of Surgery.question: 65) Which of the following increases postoperative pulmonary complications?
History, Evolution & Scope of Surgery.option3: Smoking until the day of surgery
History, Evolution & Scope of Surgery.exp: Smoking impairs mucociliary clearance and pulmonary function.

History, Evolution & Scope of Surgery.question: 66) The commonest cause of perioperative mortality in elderly surgical patients is:
History, Evolution & Scope of Surgery.exp: Cardiac events remain a major cause of perioperative mortality in high-risk patients.

History, Evolution & Scope of Surgery.question: 67) Which laboratory test is most appropriate for a patient taking warfarin?
History, Evolution & Scope of Surgery.exp: PT/INR monitors the anticoagulant effect of warfarin.

History, Evolution & Scope of Surgery.question: 68) The safest practice before surgery is to confirm:
History, Evolution & Scope of Surgery.option3: Patient identity, procedure and operative site
History, Evolution & Scope of Surgery.exp: Correct patient and correct-site verification prevents avoidable surgical errors.

History, Evolution & Scope of Surgery.question: 69) Which patient should receive venous thromboembolism prophylaxis?
History, Evolution & Scope of Surgery.option1: Healthy young patient after lipoma excision
History, Evolution & Scope of Surgery.option2: Elderly immobile patient after hip surgery
History, Evolution & Scope of Surgery.exp: Major orthopaedic surgery and prolonged immobility are major VTE risk factors.

History, Evolution & Scope of Surgery.question: 70) Which factor most delays wound healing?
History, Evolution & Scope of Surgery.exp: Infection prolongs inflammation and interferes with collagen deposition.

History, Evolution & Scope of Surgery.question: 71) Which patient is least suitable for day-care surgery?
History, Evolution & Scope of Surgery.option4: Inguinal hernia in a fit adult
History, Evolution & Scope of Surgery.exp: Major abdominal surgery requires postoperative monitoring and inpatient care.

History, Evolution & Scope of Surgery.question: 72) Which of the following is the best indicator of adequate informed consent?
History, Evolution & Scope of Surgery.option1: Patient understands the procedure and agrees voluntarily
History, Evolution & Scope of Surgery.exp: Valid consent requires understanding, capacity and voluntariness.

History, Evolution & Scope of Surgery.question: 73) Which measure most effectively reduces wrong-site surgery?
History, Evolution & Scope of Surgery.exp: The checklist improves communication and verification before incision.

History, Evolution & Scope of Surgery.question: 74) Which patient has the highest anaesthetic risk?
History, Evolution & Scope of Surgery.exp: ASA IV patients have severe systemic disease that is a constant threat to life.

History, Evolution & Scope of Surgery.question: 75) Which statement regarding elective surgery is correct ?
History, Evolution & Scope of Surgery.option1: It should proceed despite uncontrolled medical illness.
History, Evolution & Scope of Surgery.option2: Routine investigations are identical for every patient.
History, Evolution & Scope of Surgery.option3: Informed consent is optional in minor procedures.
History, Evolution & Scope of Surgery.option4: Proper patient assessment and optimisation improve surgical outcome.
History, Evolution & Scope of Surgery.exp: Individualized assessment, optimisation of comorbidities and appropriate perioperative planning are the foundations of safe elective surgery.

History, Evolution & Scope of Surgery.question: 76) Which of the following is the most important determinant of postoperative outcome?
History, Evolution & Scope of Surgery.exp: Correction of reversible medical problems before surgery significantly reduces perioperative morbidity and mortality.

History, Evolution & Scope of Surgery.question: 77) A patient taking warfarin requires elective surgery. The most appropriate investigation before operation is:
History, Evolution & Scope of Surgery.exp: PT/INR is the standard test to assess anticoagulation with warfarin.

History, Evolution & Scope of Surgery.question: 78) Which condition is associated with the highest risk of postoperative chest infection?
History, Evolution & Scope of Surgery.exp: COPD increases pulmonary complications due to impaired airway clearance and reduced respiratory reserve.

History, Evolution & Scope of Surgery.question: 79) Which patient is the best candidate for elective surgery?
History, Evolution & Scope of Surgery.exp: Elective surgery should proceed after optimization of reversible medical conditions.

History, Evolution & Scope of Surgery.question: 80) Which of the following is NOT included in preoperative assessment?
History, Evolution & Scope of Surgery.exp: Suture selection is an operative decision, not part of routine patient assessment.

History, Evolution & Scope of Surgery.question: 81) Which patient has the greatest risk of postoperative wound infection?
History, Evolution & Scope of Surgery.exp: Contaminated emergency gastrointestinal surgery carries the highest risk of surgical site infection.

History, Evolution & Scope of Surgery.question: 82) Which of the following is the commonest source of endogenous surgical wound infection?
History, Evolution & Scope of Surgery.exp: The patient’s normal flora is the commonest source of organisms causing surgical site infection.

History, Evolution & Scope of Surgery.question: 83) Which measure reduces postoperative pulmonary complications most effectively?
History, Evolution & Scope of Surgery.exp: Early mobilization improves lung expansion and reduces atelectasis.

History, Evolution & Scope of Surgery.question: 84) Which patient requires antibiotic prophylaxis before incision?
History, Evolution & Scope of Surgery.exp: Colorectal procedures have a high risk of bacterial contamination and require prophylactic antibiotics.

History, Evolution & Scope of Surgery.question: 85) The principal purpose of surgical hand preparation is to:
History, Evolution & Scope of Surgery.option4: Reduce transient flora and decrease resident flora
History, Evolution & Scope of Surgery.exp: Surgical hand preparation cannot sterilize the skin but markedly reduces bacterial load.

History, Evolution & Scope of Surgery.question: 86) Which investigation is routinely indicated before thyroid surgery?
History, Evolution & Scope of Surgery.exp: Thyroid function should be assessed before thyroid surgery to optimize perioperative management.

History, Evolution & Scope of Surgery.question: 87) Which electrolyte abnormality predisposes most strongly to cardiac arrhythmia during anaesthesia?
History, Evolution & Scope of Surgery.exp: Hypokalaemia increases myocardial excitability and the risk of arrhythmias.

History, Evolution & Scope of Surgery.question: 88) Which of the following is NOT a benefit of smoking cessation before surgery?
History, Evolution & Scope of Surgery.exp: Smoking cessation improves surgical outcomes and does not increase bleeding risk.

History, Evolution & Scope of Surgery.question: 89) Which of the following indicates poor nutritional status?
History, Evolution & Scope of Surgery.exp: Hypoalbuminaemia is associated with malnutrition and increased postoperative complications.

History, Evolution & Scope of Surgery.question: 90) Which patient should receive thromboprophylaxis with the highest priority?
History, Evolution & Scope of Surgery.option2: Elderly patient after hip fracture surgery
History, Evolution & Scope of Surgery.option3: Healthy patient after sebaceous cyst excision
History, Evolution & Scope of Surgery.exp: Major orthopaedic surgery, advanced age and immobility greatly increase VTE risk.

History, Evolution & Scope of Surgery.question: 91) Which one of the following is a component of enhanced recovery after surgery (ERAS)?
History, Evolution & Scope of Surgery.option3: Routine nasogastric tube for all patients
History, Evolution & Scope of Surgery.exp: ERAS protocols reduce complications and shorten hospital stay.

History, Evolution & Scope of Surgery.question: 92) Which of the following increases the risk of aspiration pneumonitis?
History, Evolution & Scope of Surgery.exp: Pregnancy delays gastric emptying and increases intra-abdominal pressure, raising aspiration risk.

History, Evolution & Scope of Surgery.question: 93) The WHO Surgical Safety Checklist is performed at:
History, Evolution & Scope of Surgery.exp: The checklist includes Sign In, Time Out, and Sign Out.

History, Evolution & Scope of Surgery.question: 94) Which investigation is most appropriate for assessing anaemia before elective surgery?
History, Evolution & Scope of Surgery.exp: CBC identifies anaemia and helps determine the need for optimization before surgery.

History, Evolution & Scope of Surgery.question: 95) Which patient has the highest perioperative cardiac risk?
History, Evolution & Scope of Surgery.option1: Previous myocardial infarction with heart failure
History, Evolution & Scope of Surgery.exp: Previous MI and heart failure are major predictors of perioperative cardiac complications.

History, Evolution & Scope of Surgery.question: 96) Which of the following is the best indicator of adequate preoperative preparation?
History, Evolution & Scope of Surgery.option2: Operation lasts less than one hour
History, Evolution & Scope of Surgery.option3: Patient is medically optimized for surgery
History, Evolution & Scope of Surgery.exp: The primary goal of preoperative preparation is optimization of the patient’s medical condition.

History, Evolution & Scope of Surgery.question: 97) Which patient requires informed consent from a legal guardian?
History, Evolution & Scope of Surgery.exp: Minors generally require consent from a parent or legal guardian unless emergency treatment is necessary.

History, Evolution & Scope of Surgery.question: 98) Which factor contributes most to prevention of wrong-patient surgery?
History, Evolution & Scope of Surgery.exp: Confirming patient identity using standard protocols is fundamental to surgical safety.

History, Evolution & Scope of Surgery.question: 99) Which of the following is the best marker of successful perioperative care?
History, Evolution & Scope of Surgery.exp: Successful perioperative care aims to minimize complications and improve recovery.

History, Evolution & Scope of Surgery.question: 100) Which statement regarding elective surgery is true?
History, Evolution & Scope of Surgery.option1: Healthy patients require extensive investigations before minor surgery.
History, Evolution & Scope of Surgery.option2: Preoperative evaluation should be individualized according to patient and procedure.
History, Evolution & Scope of Surgery.option3: Every patient requires ICU admission after surgery.
History, Evolution & Scope of Surgery.option4: Routine investigations should be identical for every patient.
History, Evolution & Scope of Surgery.exp: Modern perioperative care emphasizes tailored assessment based on the patient’s comorbidities, surgical risk and planned procedure rather than a fixed set of investigations.
